title: Fairness in Large Language Models in Three Hours

bias_targets.methodology: The tutorial outlines four primary methods for quantifying bias: 1) Demographic representation (analyzing the frequency of demographic word references), 2) Stereotypical association (measuring disparities in linking demographic groups to stereotyped terms), 3) Counterfactual fairness (replacing demographic identity terms in prompts to check for response invariance), and 4) Performance disparities (measuring differences in model accuracy across demographic groups on downstream tasks).

Examined through case studies of generated text, such as evaluating language models for gender stereotypes by comparing the attributes assigned in letters of recommendation for female-associated names (e.g., 'Kelly') versus male-associated names (e.g., 'Joseph'). Additionally evaluated using specific template-based datasets like WinoBias and BUG.
